title: Hide in one key, the games you haven't installed, and RustyShelf offline
highlights: X hides a game, U puts it back
Games you own but haven't installed, on the PC shelf
Internet access can be switched off
Edit a shelf: favourite or hide many games at once
IGDB for PC games, and details you type yourself

items: X on the shelf hides the chosen game, U within five seconds puts it back. On a pad, hold X to hide; a tap of X just after puts it back.
Settings → System → Internet access is on by default; off, RustyShelf reaches nothing on the Internet. A RomM server on your home network still works.
PRIVACY.md lists every site RustyShelf asks, what it sends and when.
Settings → PC → Games you haven't installed (Windows) puts the games your Playnite store libraries own on the PC shelf, greyed; Install opens Steam's install or Playnite.
Settings → Games → Edit a shelf lists every game of a shelf; left or right puts each on the shelf, among the favorites or hidden.
A PC game's description, genres, developer and dates come from IGDB too. Details → IGDB match picks the right game, Details → Edit details takes what you type.
Settings → PC → Download missing PC covers finds the best cover for each PC game, with its progress; Undo puts back what it replaced.
Settings → Collections imports Steam's collections and Playnite's categories as shelves of your own.
Details → Read manual opens a PC game's manual: one you gave it, the PDF in its folder, or the one Steam keeps.
The quick menu's Power opens into four even tiles; Restart and Shut down turn warm when chosen.
With Seamless play, a game started from its own program is followed through its folder, so a launcher that hands over and closes doesn't bring the shelf back early.

title: See a theme as you pick it, a fuller What's new, and a real disc
highlights: Picking a theme shows it on your shelf for a moment
What's new in colour, with every change of the version
The disc out of its case has a real edge and underside
A turned disc stays out of the case

items: In Settings → Look, the page fades for a moment as you change the theme, so you see it on your shelf.

After an update, a bigger card with the version's changes under New, Changed and Fixed, each in its own colour. Settings → System → What's new lists every version under its own heading, a row per change.
It has a thickness, an edge and a hole, and its underside looks like a disc's: its tracks, the mirror band round the middle and a rainbow sheen.
Comes forward as it turns, so it no longer passes into the case or the open lid.

title: Open the case, several PC games folders, and the right buttons on screen
highlights: Inspect opens the case: the disc or cartridge, and the manual inside
Zoom in to 3×, move round the box, and use the mouse
As many PC games folders as you like
Key legends show your controller's buttons, or your keyboard's

items: In Inspect, Enter opens the case and takes the disc, cartridge, UMD or floppy out; the manual's first page is inside the cover. Hold Enter with it out to play.
Zooms in to 3×; zoomed in, WASD or the left stick moves round the box. The mouse turns it, zooms and opens it; a double-click on the shelf starts it.
An Inspect tile in the quick menu, Inspect the box in Details, and V or R3 on the shelf's hint bar.
Add as many as you like and take one off, as for a console's games folders.
Opens a console game's case a step at a time; Steam and PC games still play at once.
Opens your browser on Windows, not File Explorer.
Show your controller's buttons or your keyboard's keys, not both; a controller counts from the start, and a stick alone counts too.
Lists every shelf along the top, those with only the emulator's case too.
Have a top and a bottom, so one turned on end isn't open.

title: Fixes for Trophies and manuals, and a tidier inside
highlights: Trophies' pictures come in when you switch Show
A Wrong manual that stops says so
Background work rebuilt on shared pieces

items: Switching Show between Games, Recent unlocks and Mastered no longer leaves the new rows' pictures blank.
If setting a manual aside stops half way, it says so instead of staying on Looking for another manual.
The jobs that run in the background, the ones that run a few at a time and the rows you change with ← → now share one way of working each. Nothing should look different.

title: Trophies game by game, Details in sections, and updates by themselves
highlights: Trophies: every game's achievements, each with its picture, and How to get it
Details: Read the manual beside Play, and its rows in sections
The emulator's case wears the emulator's own icon
Update by itself, from Settings → System

items: RetroAchievements, RPCS3 and Steam, each or all together; a game opens its achievements, each with its picture, rarity and points, and How to get it searches YouTube.
Read the manual beside Play, the rows below in sections, and a description that keeps its place.
A Manual tile for a game with a manual.
Settings → Look, beside All games; the first run asks for both.
On Windows, the emulator's own icon; Settings → each console → Emulator's case takes a picture of yours.
Their back of the box comes from the console game they're made from.
A game with screenshots shows its first four on the back drawn for it.
Settings → System: a newer release is downloaded, checked and used from the next start.
Opens the real screens and points at each part.
The switch is back in Settings.
The PS5's emulator, found on Linux too.
They no longer blink as you move in them.
The download says when it's saving, goes on with Settings shut, and its progress no longer covers other rows' hints.
Kept in data/ach-icons, so lists don't ask for them again.
A folder in the PC games folder holding several games gives a game for each.
Installs stopped half way no longer show up as PC games.
A LaunchBox art download or a setup brought over that stops now says so instead of hanging.
A page no longer opens with its cursor on a section's heading.

title: An installer for Windows, Accounts by service and Trophies with pictures
highlights: Windows: an installer, or a zip with the app and its data folder
Settings → Accounts: one page per service
Trophies with pictures, and Steam's rarity and points
Esc on the shelf opens the quick menu

items: RustyShelf-<version>-windows-setup.exe installs for your user alone, no admin rights; the zip holds a RustyShelf folder with the app and its data folder.
RetroAchievements, Steam, SteamGridDB, IGDB, ScreenScraper and RomM each have their own page; RetroAchievements lists whether each console's emulator is signed in.
Every sign-in and key is also written there in plain text, one per line, to edit by hand or carry to another PC.
T on the shelf opens it, with each game's icon and each achievement's badge, narrowed to RetroAchievements or Steam.
Details shows how many players have each one and its points, to sort by rarity or points.
The download shows how far it is.
Opens the quick menu instead of closing RustyShelf; Exit is under Power.
PCSX2 2.x counts as signed in with its token in secrets.ini.

title: The first stable release of the native app
highlights: The first stable release, for Windows, Linux and Android
Game streaming: games from another PC through Moonlight
Covers for Steam, store and added games, and console boxes for PC games
The Art Studio: lock a game, back to the shelf style, filters, and Art match
Less stutter on the shelf and in Settings

items: With a host PC paired in Moonlight, its games stand on a Game streaming shelf and Play opens them fullscreen; a host with a MAC address is woken first. Settings → Game streaming.
Details → Box art chooses a Steam, store or added game's cover: Steam's own, SteamGridDB's, a search under another name or a picture of yours.
A PC game can wear the box of its console release, with its back and a PC band on the spine. The PC games gallery shows every cover and where it comes from.
Backs of the box for PC games
A program put on a console's shelf gets that console's whole case, the Art Studio and manuals. Put recomps on their console's shelf can do it by itself (off by default).
Lock this game keeps every part as it is, Back to the shelf style undoes a pick, and a part's versions can be filtered by region, source, type and edition.
For a ROM hack, translation or mod: look the game up under the original's name.
G opens the Sort panel; a Menu tap or Tab opens the quick menu at the right, as in the Electron app.
Interface size, Open into, Reduce motion, Scroll speed, Controller rumble and the consoles' order.
Settings, Details and the shelf menu glide and fade as in the Electron app.
A bright pastel theme with glossy bubbles.
Zak's French merged in, with French and Turkish for the new pages.
Covers land a few at a time, settings are written off the frame, and sorting and filtering run on a worker.
Newer themes and voices no longer go back to Spectrum and Aero after a restart.

name: 0.2.0 alpha 6
title: The Electron app's look
highlights: Settings in the Electron app's look: a sidebar of tabs, a card that says what each row does
Details with the game's case beside it and a big Play button
The shelf's menu as a panel over the shelf
The first run as a card with its steps down the side

items: A sidebar of the tabs in their groups, the page's title and lead, rows with switches, a card saying what the chosen row does, and the keys in a pill. The on-screen keyboard shares the look.
The game's case on the left; its console, name, chips and a big Play button on the right, with the rest of its rows under them.
A card in the middle with its steps down the side and the keys along its foot.
RustyShelf is now the native app. The Electron app is kept on its own branch, archive/electron, and its releases stay where they are.

name: 0.1.0 alpha 5
title: Android, shelves of your own and more screenshots
highlights: The native app on Android, as an APK of its own
Shelves of your own, and automatic shelves that fill themselves
A game's Status: Not started, Playing, Finished or Abandoned
More screenshots and game info, looked up in the background
The running game's achievements in the Home menu

items: An APK beside the Windows exe: games folders picked through Android's own folder picker, games started in the console's emulator app, a controller, Back and touch.
Settings → Collections makes a shelf, searches games to put on it, renames and deletes it. A shelf can fill itself with a Status, genre or console, or the games never played.
Recently played, Most played, Playing, Finished, Never played and one per big genre, after Home.
Details sets Not started, Playing, Finished or Abandoned.
Details puts a game on another console's shelf, PC, Custom or one of your own; it still starts with its own emulator.
Games taken off their shelves are listed after the rest, to put back.
Settings → PC games: every folder in it is a game on the Ports & Recomps shelf.
Up to 12 for a console game, from ScreenScraper, libretro and IGDB, topped up in the background while nothing runs.
Over a running game: RetroAchievements, Xbox 360's from Xenia or PS3's trophies from RPCS3.
Made into manual pages from the games' own files.
Screen shape, sharp pixels and a Retro TV look for each emulator that has them.
Play asks which build to start in; Settings → Switch 2 → Emulators lists them.
An emulator that needs a BIOS it hasn't got, and IGDB for more screenshots.
Plays under the shelves the pack is the sound for.
Settings → Look → Keep themes moving while you scroll can pause a moving theme while the shelf slides.

name: 0.1.0 alpha 4
title: Settings in tabs, the Wii remote, your own sounds and seventeen themes
highlights: Alpha 3 no longer hangs at a white window on Windows
Settings in eight tabs, with what needs attention first
The Wii remote on a DolphinBar, with its pointer on the shelf
Your own sounds, a sound per console and three new voices
Seventeen new themes

items: Library, Look, Sound, Box art & media, Controls, Shelf, Accounts and System, switched with LB / RB or Page Up / Page Down. Library starts with what needs attention, each with Fix.
A new build shows its highlights once, Settings → System lists every version's notes, and a tour of the shelf runs the first time (Show the tour brings it back).
A new version copies your setup first and puts back a missing or damaged config.json; Undo the update's settings changes puts the copy back. A new RustyShelf folder offers to bring your setup over.
Nintendo and PlayStation pads during a game
Joy-Con, Pro Controller, DualShock 4 and DualSense: their quit combo closes the game and Home opens the Home menu, as an Xbox pad's do.

On a DolphinBar it drives the shelf, Settings and the Home menu, upright or sideways, with a pointer that picks a case. It's handed to Dolphin for a Wii or GameCube game, and Home held opens the Home menu.
With a Twitch developer app's Client ID and Secret (Accounts), Details fills in the description, genres, developer and release LaunchBox is missing.
Disc-era, Handheld and Living room; a sound per console; and Custom sounds from a game, a folder, a file or a ZIP.

Nebula, Abyss, Ember, Dusk, Prism, Hologram, Starfield, Rainy Night, Cherry Blossom, Snowfall, Event Horizon, Glass Lake, Neon City, Deep Sea, Thunderstorm, Fireflies and Desert Night. Pocket, Walnut, CRT and VHS are retired.
Alpha 3 could hang at a white window on Windows as it set its icon.
Its development stopped, so it's out of the native app; View opens Details again. The Electron app keeps its museum.

Kid mode
RomM's games on the shelves

The classic wall, rooms by maker or genre, the walkable arcade and the reading corner.

Attract mode and the screen dimmer

name: 0.1.0 alpha 1
title: The first alpha of RustyShelf's native app
highlights: The Rust rewrite of the Electron app: one exe for Windows
It shares the Electron app's data folder and file formats, so both can be used on the same library

items: Every console's shelf on the 3D shelf with the Electron app's layout, themes and backgrounds, Home and All shelves, Find a game, Details with game info, favourites, hidden games and collections.
Games with their emulators, the Home menu over a running game, the quit combo and Seamless play.
Downloads (libretro, LaunchBox, GameTDB, the Super Mario Wiki for Switch 2, ScreenScraper and SteamGridDB with your own account and key) and the Art Studio.
archive.org, GamesDatabase, the scan collections and PDFs drawn into pages, with the Manual Studio and the reader.
Steam and the other stores' PC games, RetroAchievements and Steam achievements, the phone companion, sounds and music, data export and the first-run setup.
